answer: A would-be attacker who wants to wander in with thousands of fake identities must post real capital for every one, and any peer can challenge a suspicious identity, burning its stake if fraud is proven. Sybil resistance here works through bonded identity: each agent must stake tokens that act as an anchor, locked for several epochs. This makes each fake account costly rather than free, so the network becomes an island of verified agents surrounded by expensive noise, and mass sock-puppet creation loses money instead of gaining influence.
